answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the release shipped (release 2h ago, latency rising 90m), making the new build the leading hypothesis rather than the daily settlement peak alone. memory_b1 is the closest precedent: a prior build was stable and rollback cleared the spike with no customer impact, which directly serves the objective of sustained availability without losing writes. I am verifying b1 before committing because the action hinges on rollback being safe for in-flight settlement writes. Other levers are weaker fits: read-replica routing (b5) offloads reads, not the write path; capacity (b3) addresses a known surge, not a post-release regression and is slow/risky mid-peak; circuit breaker (b4) targets a failing external dependency and could fail settlement writes; failover (b2) suits regional degradation. Uncertainty is preserved: peak write volume may be amplifying rather than the release causing it, so rollback should be paired with close write-latency and settlement monitoring and immediate re-evaluation if p99 does not recover.
